newsitem.title: USA: Texas Catholic church must pay $120 million for sex abuse.
newsitem.headline: Texas Catholic church must pay $120 million for sex abuse.

text.p: The Roman Catholic diocese of Dallas was ordered on Thursday to pay a record $120 million in damages to 10 former altar boys and the parents of another who were sexually abused time and again by a Catholic priest.
It was by far the largest cash penalty ever imposed against the Catholic church in a sexual abuse case.

A Dallas jury of 10 women and two men decided in a civil lawsuit that the diocese was guilty of gross negligence, malice, conspiracy and fraud in failing to stop the Rev. Rudolph Kos from abusing the children over an 11-year period ending in 1992, and in covering up evidence when the victims complained.
It said the diocese bore even more responsibility for the years of abuse than Kos himself and ordered it to pay $102 million in actual damages and $18 million in punitive damages.

"I hope they wake up the pope tonight with this," plaintiffs' attorney Sylvia Demarest told Reuters. "This verdict sends a clear message to the Catholic hierarchy of the world that this abuse must stop."
Kos' 11 victims included Jay Lemberger, a one-time altar boy who committed suicide in 1992 at the age of 20.

"My son was murdered by the Dallas diocese because they let Rudy Kos into their regime and they let him get away with this abuse," said Pat Lemberger, the boy's father. He and his wife, Nancy, joined the 10 former altar boys in the lawsuit and they were awarded a total of $20.2 million.
The boys, who now range in age from 18 to early 30s, were each awarded between $7.4 million and $13.2 million.
When the verdict was read out, the young men hugged each other and their relatives with joy.
Bishop Charles Grahmann said the church would likely appeal the damages in the hope of finding a final verdict that is "just and appropriate to the facts of the case."
The diocese argued that Kos deceived everybody, including the boys' families, and pointed out that he was suspended as soon as the first youth complained about sexual abuse in 1992.
Kos, now 52, also faces criminal charges of sexual abuse of a child. He lives in San Diego and chose not to defend himself at this civil trial.

While both Kos and the diocese are jointly responsible for the damages, the former priest has little money and plaintiffs' attorneys said they would collect "every last nickel" of the $120 million from the diocese.

Kos allegedly abused the boys on hundreds of occasions at three different Dallas churches. The plaintiffs testified that Kos was like a father to them, but drew them into sexual relationships that began with foot massages and then escalated to masturbation and oral sex.
Attorneys and church officials said the previous record for damages in a Catholic church sexual abuse case was $13 million, ordered in a Florida case last year.
